### Technical Description: Dual-Rail Breech Catch Mechanism for Semi-Automatic and Automatic Firearms

---

#### 1. Technical Field
This disclosure relates to the mechanical design of automatic and semi-automatic firearms, specifically concerning the hold-open or breech-catch assemblies used to retain the breech (slide) in a rearward, open position after the exhaustion of ammunition from a magazine.

---

#### 2. Component Architecture
The mechanism comprises three primary interacting assemblies: the **breech catch**, the **cartridge feeder** (magazine follower), and the **breech block** (slide assembly).

*   **The Breech Catch Assembly:** 
    The core of the mechanism is a specialized latch body consisting of two parallel, longitudinal rails situated along the structural frame of the firearm. These rails provide axial stability and alignment. The two rails are rigidly connected to one another by a transverse bridging element, forming a robust, unified unit. 
    
    Integrally formed on this catch assembly is an **internal projection**. This projection extends inward toward the ammunition channel, positioned vertically directly above the path of the cartridge feeder. The exterior geometry of the catch features a designated locking face along its **outer surface**, engineered to bear direct mechanical loads from the breech.

*   **The Cartridge Feeder:**
    Located within the magazine well, the spring-loaded cartridge feeder is configured to push rounds upward for chambering. In addition to feeding ammunition, its top surface serves as the mechanical actuator for the catch mechanism once the final round has cleared the magazine.

*   **The Breech Assembly:**
    The reciprocating breech features an integrated **feeding bridge**—a structural cross-member responsible for stripping rounds from the magazine during the forward return stroke. The lower interface of this feeding bridge is dimensioned to clear the catch during normal operation, but to engage the outer surface of the catch when the catch is pivoted upward.

---

#### 3. Method of Operation

##### A. Standard Cycling (Cartridges Present)
During normal operation, cartridges remaining in the magazine press downward against the cartridge feeder, keeping it depressed beneath the activation threshold. The breech catch rests in a lowered, disengaged position, allowing the breech and its feeding bridge to cycle back and forth unhindered over the catch during firing and reloading strokes.

##### B. Engagement Sequence (Last Cartridge Exchanged)
1. **Actuation:** Upon the feeding and firing of the final cartridge in the magazine, the cartridge feeder is propelled to its topmost vertical limit by the magazine spring.
2. **Impulse Transfer:** As the feeder reaches this peak position, its upper surface impacts the bottom of the catch’s **internal projection**, applying direct upward force.
3. **Pivoting/Tilting:** This upward thrust forces the entire breech catch assembly—supported by its two longitudinal rails—to tilt on its pivot axis. The upward tilt elevates the outer surface of the catch into the recoil path of the breech.

##### C. Locking the Breech
As the firearm completes its final stroke, the breech moves rearward under recoil forces and then begins its forward movement. As it attempts to return forward:
* The **feeding bridge** of the breech strikes the exposed **outer surface** of the now-tilted catch.
* The mechanical interference between the feeding bridge and the catch halts the forward momentum of the breech, firmly locking it in its fully rearward position.

---

#### 4. System Advantages
By utilizing dual longitudinal rails connected by a transverse bridge, the mechanism distributes structural stress evenly across both sides of the receiver frame, preventing binding or tilting off-axis. Furthermore, the direct interaction between the internal projection and the cartridge feeder eliminates the need for complex intermediate levers, maximizing mechanical reliability and reducing component wear.

counterfactuals.output:
# Technical Engineering Description: Dual-Rail Bridged Last-Round Slide-Lock Mechanism

**Document ID:** ENG-MECH-LRSL-004  
**Classification:** Mechanical System Architecture Specification  
**Subject:** Dual Longitudinal Rail and Transverse Bridge Slide Retention System  

---

## 1. System Overview

The Dual-Rail Bridged Last-Round Slide-Lock Mechanism is an electromechanical or pure mechanical sub-assembly designed to hold a firearm’s slide in its rearmost position following the depletion of the final cartridge in a magazine. 

Unlike traditional single-point slide stops—which suffer from asymmetrical torsional loading and uneven frame wear—this design utilizes a symmetrical architecture consisting of **two parallel longitudinal guide rails** rigidized by a **transverse cross-bridge**. This structural frame provides dual-plane engagement, balanced shear-load distribution, and enhanced reliability under severe fouling and high recoil impulses.

```
       [ Slide Reciprocation Vector ] <===================>
       ____________________________________________________
      |                    FIREARM SLIDE                   |
      |___                                              ___|
          |  [Slide Notch L]          [Slide Notch R]  |
          |_______  ______________________  ___________|
                  ||                      ||
  ==========[ Left Rail ]=============[ Right Rail ]==========  <-- Dual Longitudinal Rails
                  ||     |          |     ||
                  ||=====|  BRIDGE  |=====||                    <-- Transverse Bridge
                         |__________|
                              ^
                    [ Magazine Follower ]
```

---

## 2. Component Breakdown & Geometry

### 2.1 Dual Longitudinal Rails (Primary Actuators)
*   **Orientation:** Positioned parallel to the bore axis along the interior or exterior guide channels of the frame (left and right flanks).
*   **Geometry:** Precision-machined or metal-injection-molded (MIM) steel bars featuring:
    *   **Bearing Surfaces:** Ground planar faces that constrain movement to vertical linear translation (or low-angle rotational arc) relative to the frame.
    *   **Engagement Arrestors (Lugs):** Upward-facing shoulder surfaces located at the upper margin of each rail designed to interlock with corresponding left and right arresting notches in the slide.
*   **Function:** Transmit vertical motion from the bridge into the path of the slide and absorb the forward kinetic energy of the returning slide.

### 2.2 Transverse Bridge (Kinematic Interface)
*   **Orientation:** Perpendicular to the longitudinal rails, spanning the width of the magazine well within the receiver architecture.
*   **Geometry:** A contoured cross-member rigidly affixed to (or integral with) both longitudinal rails, forming a rigid **"H-frame" or "U-bracket"** geometry.
*   **Function:**
    *   Serves as the contact surface for the magazine follower’s lift-tab.
    *   Mechanically couples the left and right rails to eliminate independent twisting or differential binding (prevents mechanical cocking/jamming).

### 2.3 System Return Spring
*   A low-rate torsion or compression spring acting upon the bridge-rail assembly. It applies a continuous downward bias force ($F_{return}$), maintaining the mechanism in a neutral (disengaged) state during normal firing.

---

## 3. Kinematic Sequence of Operation

```
+-------------------+     +-------------------+     +-------------------+
|  1. NEUTRAL STATE | --> | 2. ACTUATION STATE| --> |3. ENGAGEMENT STATE|
|  Live rounds in   |     | Follower contacts |     | Rails rise into   |
|  magazine.        |     | bridge.           |     | slide notches.    |
+-------------------+     +-------------------+     +-------------------+
```

### Phase 1: Neutral / Firing State (Cartridges Present)
1. **Constraint:** Loaded cartridges in the magazine hold the magazine follower below the vertical plane of the transverse bridge.
2. **State:** The return spring biases the dual longitudinal rails to their bottom dead center (BDC) position.
3. **Slide Kinematics:** The slide cycles freely over the dual rails during recoil and battery return without interference. Clearance is maintained via defined vertical keep-out zones.

### Phase 2: Terminal Elevation (Last Round Expended)
1. **Triggering Event:** The final cartridge is stripped from the magazine feed lips and chambered. The magazine follower reaches its upper limit of travel driven by the magazine tube spring force ($F_{mag}$).
2. **Contact:** The lifting lug of the empty magazine follower contacts the underside of the **transverse bridge**.
3. **Force Balance Condition:**
   $$F_{mag} > F_{return} + F_{friction}$$
   *Where $F_{mag}$ is the remaining force of the magazine spring, $F_{return}$ is the slide lock return spring force, and $F_{friction}$ is the static friction of the system tracks.*

### Phase 3: Vertical Translation & Lockup
1. **Translation:** As the slide travels rearward under blowback/recoil momentum, clearing the ejection port, the follower pushes the transverse bridge upward.
2. **Symmetrical Lift:** The bridge translates this upward vector equally into both the left and right longitudinal rails, lifting them simultaneously along their frame-guided vertical slots.
3. **Interlock:** As the slide completes its rearward stroke and begins moving forward under recoil spring pressure, the engagement lugs of both longitudinal rails align with and enter the corresponding left and right slide notches.
4. **Energy Dissipation:** The forward momentum of the slide is arrested simultaneously on both sides. The impact energy ($E_k$) is evenly split between the two longitudinal rails and transferred symmetrically into the frame rails.

---

## 4. Mechanical Advantages & Structural Dynamics

### 4.1 Moment-Free Load Transfer
In single-lever slide catches, the force of the slide striking a single lug creates an off-axis moment arm ($M = F \cdot d$), inducing rotational torque across the pivot pin and bending stresses in the frame. 

The **dual-rail bridge system** creates a closed-loop force path:
$$\sum M_z = 0$$
By arresting the slide on both sides of its centerline simultaneously, the system eliminates yawing moments on the slide and twisting moments on the frame, significantly increasing component fatigue life.

### 4.2 Reduced Surface Contact Pressure
By doubling the engagement area ($A_{total} = A_{left\_lug} + A_{right\_lug}$), the operational shear stress ($\tau$) on the locking interfaces is reduced by approximately 50%:
$$\tau = \frac{F_{slide}}{2 \cdot A_{lug}}$$
This prevents peening, deformation, and rounding of the slide catch notches over high round counts.

### 4.3 FOULING IMMUNITY VIA BRIDGE STIFFNESS
The transverse bridge acts as a torsional stiffener. If carbon fouling or debris enters one longitudinal rail slot, the lifting force transmitted from the opposite side via the rigid bridge forces the system through the obstruction, preventing single-sided binding or partial engagement failures.

---

## 5. Manual Reset & Disengagement

1. **Magazine Extraction:** Removing the empty magazine relieves the upward force ($F_{mag}$) from the bridge. However, friction caused by the forward force of the slide against the engagement lugs holds the mechanism in place (friction lock).
2. **Reset Method A (Slide Pull):** Retracting the slide slightly rearward removes the forward force from the rail lugs. The return spring instantly pulls the bridge-and-rail assembly down to BDC.
3. **Reset Method B (Manual Override):** Depression of an external thumb interface mechanically linked to one (or both) longitudinal rails creates a downward force ($F_{manual}$) that overcomes the friction threshold, sliding the engagement surfaces out of the slide notches and releasing the slide into battery.

---

## 6. Engineering Summary Table

| Parameter | Specification / Attribute |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Kinematic Type** | Guided Dual-Linear / Parallel Arc Translation |
| **Force Input Point** | Center/Off-Center Transverse Bridge via Follower Lug |
| **Force Output Points** | Dual Symmetrical Engagement Lugs |
| **Primary Stress Mode** | Direct Shear (Lugs), Bending/Torsion (Bridge) |
| **Key Failure Mode Prevented** | Slide Catch Peening, Asymmetrical Frame Twist, Failure to Lock on Last Round (FTL) |
| **Material Recommendation** | AISI 4140/4340 Alloy Steel (Heat treated to 45–50 HRC) or 17-4 PH Stainless Steel |

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a pistol breech catch mechanism.
counterfactuals.output:
A **pistol breech catch mechanism**—more commonly referred to as a **slide stop**, **slide catch**, or **slide release**—is a mechanical component in semi-automatic handguns. Its primary function is to lock the breech (slide) in the open position after the last cartridge in the magazine has been fired, or when manually operated by the shooter.

Here is a detailed breakdown of its components, how it works, and its mechanical purpose.

---

### 1. Key Components

The mechanism consists of a few interacting parts located between the frame, the slide, and the magazine:

*   **The Slide Catch Lever:** A spring-loaded metal lever mounted on the handgun’s frame (usually on the side). It features an external tab for thumb operation and an internal projection that extends into the magazine well.
*   **The Pivot Pin:** The lever rotates around a pin (often integral to the catch). In many designs (like the M1911 or CZ-75), this pin also passes through the barrel link, serving double duty as a frame assembly pin.
*   **The Slide Notch:** A precisely cut recess on the bottom edge of the slide.
*   **The Magazine Follower:** The spring-loaded plastic or metal platform inside the magazine that pushes cartridges upward. It features a small ledge designed to contact the internal projection of the slide catch.
*   **Detent Spring:** A small spring or detent plunger that applies subtle downward pressure on the lever, preventing it from bouncing up and locking the slide prematurely during normal firing.

---

### 2. How the Mechanism Operates

The operation of a slide catch can be broken down into three main phases:

#### Phase A: Normal Firing (Cartridges Present)
1. When cartridges are in the magazine, they sit on top of the magazine follower.
2. The cartridges push the follower down, away from the internal tab of the slide catch lever.
3. The small detent spring keeps the slide catch in the **down position**.
4. As the gun is fired, the slide cycles backward and forward freely over the catch without engaging it.

#### Phase B: The Last Round (Automatic Lock-Back)
1. When the final round is fired, the slide travels backward, extracting and ejecting the empty casing.
2. With no cartridges remaining in the magazine, the **magazine follower rises to its highest point**.
3. A small tab on the rising follower pushes **upward** against the internal projection of the slide catch lever, overcoming the light tension of the detent spring.
4. As the slide attempts to return forward under the pressure of the recoil spring, the upward-tilted slide catch lever aligns with and drops into the **slide notch**.
5. The forward momentum of the slide is physically blocked by the catch, leaving the action open.

#### Phase C: Releasing the Breech
To chamber a new round after inserting a fresh magazine, the shooter has two options to release the catch:
1. **Manual Lever Release:** The shooter presses down on the external tab of the slide catch lever. This forces the catch out of the slide notch, allowing the recoil spring to drive the slide forward, stripping a new cartridge from the magazine into the chamber.
2. **"Slingshot" Method:** The shooter pulls the slide slightly further to the rear by hand. This relieves the friction holding the catch inside the notch. The detent spring pushes the catch back down, and releasing the slide allows it to spring forward into battery.

---

### 3. Purpose and Benefits

The breech catch mechanism serves three critical roles in firearm operation:

*   **Tactical/Speed Advantage:** It drastically speeds up reloading. The shooter can visually confirm the gun is empty, insert a fresh magazine, and release the slide without having to fully rack it by hand.
*   **Safety Indication:** Holding the action open provides a clear visual indicator to the shooter and surrounding individuals that the firearm is empty and the chamber is clear.
*   **Mechanical Safety:** In the event of a malfunction, locking the slide open allows the shooter to inspect the chamber, clear jams, or drop the magazine safely.

---

### 4. Variations in Design

*   **Internal Slide Stops:** Some older or compact designs (like the Walther PPK) have an internal slide catch. The slide locks back when empty, but there is no external lever; inserting a new magazine and pulling the slide back slightly is the only way to release it.
*   **Ambidextrous Catches:** Modern duty pistols (e.g., Glock Gen 5, SIG Sauer P320) feature dual-sided levers so the catch can be operated easily by left- or right-handed shooters.

### **PATENT TECHNICAL SUMMARY**

**Title:** Hold-Open Mechanism for Firearm Breech Assembly  
**Field of the Invention:** Firearm cycling and magazine interaction mechanisms.

---

### **System Architecture**
The mechanism comprises a receiver frame (10), a reciprocating breech block (12) defining an engagement notch (14) on its underside or lateral face, a removable magazine (16), and a pivotable or translatable breech catch (24). 

The magazine (16) houses a spring-loaded cartridge feeder (18) driven vertically by a magazine spring (20). The cartridge feeder (18) includes an integral actuating lug (22) projecting laterally through an opening in the magazine wall. 

The breech catch (24) is mounted to the receiver frame (10) via a pivot pin (26) and includes an internal contact arm (28) extending into the path of the feeder actuating lug (22), and an external locking lug (30) configured to engage the engagement notch (14) of the breech block (12). A light return spring (32) biases the breech catch (24) downward into a default disengaged position.

```
       [ Reciprocating Breech Block (12) ]
              |___ Notch (14) ___
                                 |
 [ Breech Catch (24) ] <--- Pushed UPWARD
        |-- Contact Arm (28)
        ^
 [ Actuating Lug (22) ]
 [ Cartridge Feeder (18) ] <--- Driven UPWARD after last round
 [ Magazine Spring (20) ]
```

---

### **Kinematics and Operational Sequence**

1. **Loaded Operation:**  
   During normal firing while cartridges are present in the magazine (16), the column of ammunition depresses the cartridge feeder (18). The actuating lug (22) remains positioned below the contact arm (28) of the breech catch (24). The return spring (32) holds the breech catch (24) in its lowered position, allowing the breech block (12) to cycle freely back and forth over the mechanism.

2. **Last-Round Actuation:**  
   Upon discharge and ejection of the final cartridge, the breech block (12) travels rearward to its point of maximum recoil. With no remaining cartridges to constrain it, the magazine spring (20) expands, driving the cartridge feeder (18) upward to its maximum vertical limit within the magazine (16).

3. **Upward Displacement of the Catch:**  
   As the cartridge feeder (18) reaches its top-of-travel position, the actuating lug (22) directly impacts the contact arm (28) of the breech catch (24). The expansion force of the magazine spring (20)—acting through the feeder (18)—overcomes the lesser force of the return spring (32), forcing the breech catch (24) to pivot/translate **upward** around the pivot pin (26).

4. **Breech Lockout:**  
   The upward displacement elevates the locking lug (30) directly into the stroke path of the breech block (12). As the breech block (12) attempts its forward return stroke under counter-recoil force, the engagement notch (14) impacts the raised locking lug (30). The mechanical interference between the locking lug (30) and the notch (14) arrests forward movement, securely locking the breech block (12) in the open, rearward position.

---

### **Key Inventive Claim Elements**
* Direct kinetic transfer from the magazine feeder (18) via an actuating lug (22) to lift the breech catch (24) upward.
* Passive automatic displacement of the catch locking lug (30) into the recoil path of the breech block (12) solely triggered by the depletion of ammunition.
* Unlocking occurs automatically upon magazine removal or manual displacement of the catch (24), overcoming the contact interface.

### **TITLE OF THE INVENTION**
**AUTOMATIC SLIDE RETENTION ASSEMBLY FOR SEMI-AUTOMATIC FIREARMS RESPONSIVE TO MAGAZINE DEPLETION**

---

### **ABSTRACT**
A slide retention mechanism for a semi-automatic firearm configured to automatically arrest the forward travel of a reciprocating slide upon the depletion of ammunition from an inserted magazine. The system utilizes kinetic energy stored within a magazine spring to displace a follower into direct mechanical engagement with an internal actuation shelf of a pivotable slide catch lever. Upon final round ejection, the catch lever elevates a locking lug into the longitudinal travel path of the slide, establishing a geometric interference fit with a corresponding notch formed in the slide body, thereby locking the action in an open state.

---

### **1. SYSTEM COMPONENTS & NOMENCLATURE**

```
[100] Reciprocating Slide          [200] Firearm Frame/Receiver
  ├── [102] Slide Catch Notch        ├── [202] Transverse Pivot Axis
  └── [104] Recoil Spring            └── [204] Detent Assembly
[300] Ammunition Magazine          [400] Breech Catch Lever
  ├── [302] Magazine Tube            ├── [402] Pivot Shaft / Pin
  ├── [304] Follower                 ├── [404] Internal Actuation Shelf
  ├── [306] Follower Actuation Tab   ├── [406] External Locking Lug
  └── [308] Magazine Spring          └── [408] Manual Release Paddle
```

---

### **2. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS**

#### **2.1 Spatial and Structural Arrangement**
Referring to the structural assembly:
*   The **Reciprocating Slide [100]** is slidably mounted on parallel guide rails of the **Frame [200]** and is continuously biased toward a forward (in-battery) position via a **Recoil Spring [104]**. The slide contains a downwardly facing notch designated as the **Slide Catch Notch [102]**.
*   The **Breech Catch Lever [400]** is pivotally mounted to the frame via a **Pivot Shaft [402]** oriented perpendicular to the firearm's longitudinal axis of fire.
*   The **Breech Catch Lever [400]** comprises two primary functional extensions relative to its pivot axis:
    1.  An **Internal Actuation Shelf [404]**, protruding laterally into the internal magazine well cavity.
    2.  An **External Locking Lug [406]**, positioned externally or semi-externally, aligned with the longitudinal track of the **Slide Catch Notch [102]**.
*   The lever is normally maintained in a disengaged (lowered) state by a secondary force—either gravity or a light **Detent Assembly [204]** (e.g., a detent pin or spring wire)—which provides a downward biasing force ($F_{\text{detent}}$).

```
                      +-------------------+ (Slide [100])
                      |      [102] Notch  |
                      +-------+   +-------+
                              |   | <--- [406] Locking Lug (Rises into path)
    +-------------------------+---+--------------------------+
    |                                                        |
    |                   [400] Catch Lever                    |
    |  [402] Pivot          [404] Actuation Shelf            |
    |    (O)-----------------------[ ]                       |
    +-------------------------------|------------------------+
                                    ^ 
                                    | Upward force from [306]
                             +--------------+
                             | [304] Follower
                             +--------------+ (Magazine)
```

---

### **3. MECHANICAL OPERATION & KINETIC WORKFLOW**

The cycle of operation functions through three sequential mechanical states:

#### **State A: Ammunition Present (Disengaged State)**
When one or more cartridges are present within the **Magazine Tube [302]**, the stack of ammunition depresses the **Follower [304]** against the compression of the **Magazine Spring [308]**. 

In this state, the **Follower Actuation Tab [306]** remains spatially isolated below the **Internal Actuation Shelf [404]**. The **Breech Catch Lever [400]** rests at its downward limit of travel due to $F_{\text{detent}}$. The **Reciprocating Slide [100]** cycles freely rearward (under recoil forces) and forward (under recoil spring expansion) without mechanical interference from the **Locking Lug [406]**.

#### **State B: Depletion Transition State (Initiation)**
Upon the discharge and subsequent extraction/ejection of the final cartridge in the magazine:
1.  The **Magazine Spring [308]** expands upward, driving the unloaded **Follower [304]** to the top of its stroke within the **Magazine Tube [302]**.
2.  As the follower reaches its terminal vertical position, the **Follower Actuation Tab [306]** contacts the underside of the **Internal Actuation Shelf [404]**.
3.  The upward vertical force exerted by the magazine spring ($F_{\text{mag}}$) exceeds the downward force of the detent ($F_{\text{detent}}$):
    $$\sum F_{\text{vertical}} = F_{\text{mag}} - F_{\text{detent}} > 0$$
4.  This net upward force creates a mechanical moment around the **Pivot Shaft [402]**, rotating the entire **Breech Catch Lever [400]** upward by a predetermined angular displacement ($\theta$).

#### **State C: Lockout (Geometric Interference)**
1.  During this moment of ejection, the **Slide [100]** is at its maximum rearward recoil position.
2.  The rotation ($\theta$) elevates the **External Locking Lug [406]** directly into the forward travel path of the **Slide Catch Notch [102]**.
3.  As the **Recoil Spring [104]** attempts to drive the slide forward into battery, the vertical face of the **Slide Catch Notch [102]** impacts the bearing face of the elevated **Locking Lug [406]**.
4.  **Static Friction Lockup:** The horizontal force exerted by the recoil spring ($F_{\text{recoil}}$) creates high static friction ($f_s$) at the interface between the locking lug and the slide notch:
    $$f_s = \mu_s \cdot F_{\text{recoil}}$$
    This force differential mechanically binds the catch lever in its upward position, arresting all forward motion of the slide and exposing the empty chamber for clearing or reloading.

---

### **4. MANUAL AND SYSTEM RECOVERY (RESETTING)**

To disengage the lock open mechanism, two pathways exist:

1.  **Manual Lever Actuation:** The user depresses the **Manual Release Paddle [408]** with sufficient downward force to overcome the static frictional force ($f_s$) generated by the recoil spring. Once overcome, the slide moves forward into battery.
2.  **Slide Retraction (Power Stroke):** Retracting the slide manually rearward relieves the normal force ($F_{\text{recoil}}$) exerted on the **Locking Lug [406]**, dropping $f_s$ to zero. 
    *   If a fresh, loaded magazine is inserted, the follower tab [306] is depressed out of contact with shelf [404]. The **Detent Assembly [204]** biases the catch lever down, removing the lug [406] from the slide track. Releasing the slide allows it to chamber a new round.

---

### **CLAIMS (PATENT-STYLE DEFINITION)**

**What is claimed is:**

1.  **A slide lock assembly for a firearm comprising:**
    *   A frame;
    *   A slide mounted to said frame configured to reciprocate along a longitudinal axis, said slide comprising a lock notch;
    *   A removable magazine containing a spring-biased follower, said follower comprising a lateral projection; and
    *   A catch lever pivotally coupled to said frame, having an internal arm positioned within a travel path of said lateral projection and an external lug positioned adjacent to said slide;
    *   *wherein* upward displacement of said follower upon ejection of a final cartridge causes said lateral projection to lift said internal arm, rotating said external lug into engagement with said slide lock notch to arrest forward travel of said slide.
